project: Project Maven (Algorithmic Warfare Cross-Functional Team - AWCFT)
actors: US Army (160th Special Operations Aviation Regiment)
vendor_model: Various computer vision algorithms, AI/ML models for predictive maintenance; Google (initial involvement)
use_case: Automated Processing, Exploitation, and Dissemination (PED) of full-motion video (FMV) for intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) assets, using computer vision for object detection, classification, and alerts. Expanded scope includes predictive maintenance for aircraft, cybersecurity, and monitoring special operators' brain health.
summary: Project Maven is a foundational DoD effort that leverages general-purpose AI/ML, primarily computer vision, to automate intelligence analysis from full-motion video and has expanded to include predictive maintenance and other operational support functions.
description: Launched in April 2017, Project Maven was a foundational DoD effort to accelerate the integration of big data, AI, and machine learning into its programs. Its initial objective was to automate the processing, exploitation, and dissemination (PED) of full-motion video (FMV) collected by intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) assets, primarily using computer vision algorithms for object detection, classification, and alerts. This involved bringing industry-best software in AI and computer vision to FMV, fielding it to warfighters, gathering feedback, and rapidly upgrading the tools' performance. While initially focused on FMV analysis for counterinsurgency and counterterrorism operations, its scope quickly expanded to include broader applications such as predictive maintenance for aircraft (e.g., for the Army's 160th Special Operations Aviation Regiment), cybersecurity, and even monitoring special operators' brain health. The project faced early challenges, including data fragmentation and issues with algorithm accuracy (around 50% for geo-referencing), which led to the adoption of a 'field to learn' approach and the development of new human-machine interfaces to improve utility. By Spring 2018, significant progress was reported, with AI acting as a 'combat multiplier' by freeing human analysts to focus on more complex tasks. Project Maven was explicitly identified as a key 'National Mission Initiative' for the newly established Joint Artificial Intelligence Center (JAIC).

actors: US Armed Forces (Army, Air Force, Navy, Marines, Coast Guard)
vendor_model: AI-enabled command and control systems, data integration platforms
use_case: Integrating communication networks of all US Armed Forces branches into a larger, all-spatial-scale network ('Connect every sensor, every shooter') to enable global data movement and real-time decision support.
summary: JADC2 is a cross-service initiative leveraging AI to integrate military communication networks for global data movement and enhanced decision-making.
description: Joint All-Domain Command and Control (JADC2) is an ambitious initiative aiming to integrate the communication networks of all US Armed Forces branches (Army, Air Force, Navy, Marines, and Coast Guard) into a larger, all-spatial-scale network, with the tagline 'Connect every sensor, every shooter,' enabling global data movement. AI is critical to process the massive data flows and provide real-time decision support within this integrated network. By February 2024, the DoD announced it had achieved a 'minimum viable capability' in JADC2.

vendor_model: Data analytics and AI tools for workflow improvement
use_case: Identifying and overcoming barriers to data sharing across the Joint force, demonstrating how data, analytics, and AI can improve Joint workflows for various missions, from global integrated deterrence to targeting and fires.
summary: GIDEs are a series of CDAO-led experiments demonstrating how AI and data analytics can improve joint military operations and overcome data sharing barriers.
description: The CDAO announced a series of ongoing GIDEs in January 2023. These experiments are designed to identify and overcome barriers in policy, security, connectivity, and user-interface that hinder data sharing across the Joint force, and to demonstrate how data, analytics, and AI can improve Joint workflows for various missions, from global integrated deterrence to targeting and fires. By July 2024, 11 GIDEs had been conducted, with another scheduled for March-April 2025.

vendor_model: Cloud-based AI development and experimentation platform
use_case: Providing a cloud-based platform for AI development, experimentation, and deployment across the entire DoD.
summary: The JCF is the DoD's cloud-based platform for developing and experimenting with AI solutions across the department.
description: The Joint Common Foundation (JCF) is explicitly described as 'The DoD's Cloud-Based AI Development and Experimentation Platform'. JCF represents a critical piece of general-purpose AI infrastructure, providing a shared, scalable environment for developing, testing, and deploying AI solutions across the entire Department of Defense.

project: Neuromorphic Computing and Edge AI Initiatives
vendor_model: Neuromorphic processors, neural network computation capabilities for edge devices
use_case: Performing neural network computations directly on sensors in weapon systems and military vehicles (edge computing) to increase combat network robustness by reducing the need for central data processing.
summary: JAIC is exploring neuromorphic computing for edge AI to enable on-sensor processing and enhance combat network robustness.
description: JAIC expressed primary interest in edge computing, particularly leveraging neuromorphic processors to perform neural network computations directly on sensors. This approach aims to increase the robustness of combat networks by reducing the need to send data to a central processor, thus enabling faster, more resilient AI operations at the tactical edge.

project: Military AI Prototypes (OpenAI Public Sector LLC Contract)
vendor_model: OpenAI frontier AI capabilities, foundation models (GPT-4 derivatives)
use_case: Designing military AI prototypes to meet critical national security needs for combat operations and Pentagon internal management systems. Includes multisource data mining in conflict zones (satellite imagery, sensors, drones), decision support in tactical contexts, prediction of adversarial behavior via algorithmic simulation, and automated logistics optimization in contested environments.
summary: OpenAI Public Sector LLC received a $200M contract from the Pentagon to develop frontier AI prototypes for combat and internal management, focusing on data mining, decision support, and logistics.
description: In a landmark development, OpenAI Public Sector LLC was awarded a $200 million contract by the US Department of Defense (Pentagon) to design military artificial intelligence prototypes. This project, set to run until July 2026, aims to meet critical national security needs for both combat operations and the Pentagon's internal management systems. The partnership specifically leverages 'frontier AI' and 'foundation models' (likely derived from OpenAI's GPT-4 and its specialized derivatives) for advanced capabilities such as multisource data mining in conflict zones, decision support in tactical contexts, prediction of adversarial behavior via algorithmic simulation, and automated logistics optimization in contested environments.

project: Expansion of Advanced AI Capabilities (CDAO Contracts)
actors: Pentagon's Chief Digital and AI Office (CDAO)
vendor_model: Google AI, xAI Grok for Government, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT models
use_case: Developing agentic AI workflows for key national security missions, including intelligence analysis, campaigning, logistics, and data collection. Builds upon existing uses of generative AI tools for tasks like tech support and finding files.
summary: The CDAO awarded up to $200M each to Google, xAI, Anthropic, and OpenAI to develop advanced agentic AI for national security missions like intelligence, logistics, and data collection.
description: On July 15, 2025, the Pentagon's Chief Digital and AI Office (CDAO) announced that it had chosen Google, xAI, Anthropic, and OpenAI to help the US military expand its use of 'advanced artificial intelligence capabilities'. Each company received a contract worth up to $200 million. These firms are tasked with developing 'agentic AI workflows' for key national security missions. While the Pentagon did not specify all missions, the department has indicated interest in areas like intelligence analysis, campaigning, logistics, and data collection, building upon existing uses of generative AI tools for tasks such as tech support and finding files. Notably, Elon Musk-owned xAI unveiled its 'Grok for Government' production line following this announcement.

use_case: Ingesting and consolidating data from government and commercial sensors to support space domain awareness missions. Facilitates data sharing across the Space Force enterprise (tactical, operational, strategic levels) and with Combatant Commands, commercial entities, and partner nations.
summary: The UDL is a cloud-based data repository, launched in 2018, that consolidates sensor data for Space Force domain awareness and facilitates AI-driven analysis.
description: A key component of the Space Force's strategy, the UDL is a cloud-based data repository launched in 2018 by the Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL). It is designed to ingest and consolidate data from both government and commercial sensors to support space domain awareness missions. Following a 2023 Government Accountability Office (GAO) report that highlighted challenges, the UDL transitioned from a prototype to an official Program of Record on November 13, 2024, with ongoing efforts to identify and expose more sensor data for analysis by the National Space Intelligence Center and integrate it into Space Operations Squadrons.

vendor_model: Internal AFRL expertise, collaborations with academic and commercial AI researchers
use_case: Operationalizing AI at scale for the Air Force and Space Force. Focuses on human-autonomy teams (HATs), safe autonomy, reinforcement training for AI-based tactical autopilots, and neuroscience-informed AI.
summary: ACT3 is an AFRL AI special operations organization tasked with operationalizing AI at scale for the Air and Space Forces, focusing on human-autonomy teams and safe AI.
description: The Air Force Research Laboratory's (AFRL) Autonomy Capability Team (ACT3) is an 'AI Special Operations organization' specifically tasked with operationalizing AI at scale for both the Air Force and the Space Force. It employs an innovative 'start-up' business model, integrating AFRL's internal expertise with collaborations from leading academic and commercial AI researchers worldwide.

project: Air and Space Force Cognitive Engine (ASCE)
vendor_model: Software suite for AI development on Kubernetes clusters
use_case: Enables users (Airmen) to develop complex AI solutions at any scale. Applicable to diverse requirements including business processes (civilian hiring, contract monitoring), predictive maintenance, automated air combat operations, aircraft damage inspection, humanitarian assistance, disaster relief, additive manufacturing, and intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) missions.
summary: ASCE is an AFRL-developed, license-free software suite enabling Airmen to develop and deploy complex AI solutions for a wide range of operational and business needs.
description: Developed by ACT3, ASCE is described as a 'one-stop, all-inclusive, license-free suite of closely integrated software and services that enable users to develop complex AI solutions at any scale' on top of any Kubernetes cluster. Its vision is to make AI a 'do-it-yourself tool for every Airman,' applicable to a remarkably diverse range of requirements, including business processes (e.g., civilian hiring, contract monitoring), predictive maintenance, automated air combat operations, aircraft damage inspection, humanitarian assistance, disaster relief, additive manufacturing, and intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) missions.
